correctness.rationale: The published iterate formula gives \(d_k=(1,\ldots,1,-(k-1),0,\ldots,0)\). These vectors have exact squared lengths \(k(k-1)\) and pairwise zero dot products. The resulting right-simplex coordinates give the inradius by normalized facet clearance. For the minimum sphere, the displayed positive weights sum to one, all active vertices have equal distance, every inactive vertex is no farther away, and the weighted parallel-axis identity proves global optimality and center uniqueness. The contact transition follows exactly from equality in the inactive-distance inequality.

value.rationale: The distinguished permutation \(23\cdots n1\) is the primary special family in the source literature. Recognizing its stack-sorting simplex as a right simplex gives a complete Euclidean metric model not supplied by the lattice-equivalence theory. The minimum-enclosing sphere is especially nontrivial: from dimension three onward it is supported by only a tail of the iterates, and its contact number has an exact triangular-number phase transition. This is a family-wide structural theorem rather than a low-dimensional calculation.
